articles.title: Signed, Sealed, Leaked: Trust Beyond Signature for MCP Toolchains
articles.excerpt: Code signing proves who built a tool. It does not prove what the tool does at runtime. A legitimately signed MCP server can perform its advertised function while exfiltrating conversation history, API…
articles.body: Code signing proves who built a tool. It does not prove what the tool does at runtime. A legitimately signed MCP server can perform its advertised function while exfiltrating conversation history, API keys, or intermediate state to a policy-allowed destination. Recent breaches (Hugging Face agent intrusion, Railway/Primcloud compromise, Postman plugin modification) demonstrate that signature verification is table stakes, not a solution. A new ArXiv paper (2611.06585v1) exposes this trust gap and introduces germline execution , a runtime isolation model that limits information disclosure without inspecting tool implementations. The approach forks ephemeral process copies from a data-free germline, each receiving only the data authorized for its destination.

articles.title: Web Scraping for RAG: Build a Reliable Pipeline with Zyte API, Qdrant and LangChain
articles.excerpt: Web scraping for RAG looks simple until the pipeline fails without telling anyone: a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline that reads from the public web can get a 403 from a bot check, or a 2…
articles.body: Web scraping for RAG looks simple until the pipeline fails without telling anyone: a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline that reads from the public web can get a 403 from a bot check, or a 200 that contains an empty JavaScript shell, and the pipeline either indexes that shell as if it were a real page or keeps serving last month's copy, while the chatbot on top answers with the same confidence it had when the data was good. This article builds the backend of a chat help bot for an online bookstore: a small, tested Python pipeline built on LangChain , Qdrant , and Zyte API that treats a blocked or empty page as a first-class outcome, fetches pages as LLM-ready Markdown, and refuses to let a bad fetch replace good data in the vector store.

articles.title: Safe Tools, Unsafe Session: Why Agent Permissions Need History
articles.excerpt: I connected Claude Code to my Gmail through a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server so it could triage my inbox. The same session can run Bash, because that's how it runs my tests. I'm comfortable with…
articles.body: I connected Claude Code to my Gmail through a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server so it could triage my inbox. The same session can run Bash , because that's how it runs my tests. I'm comfortable with each of those on its own. Put them in one context window, though, and an email that says "run this one-liner to confirm your account" becomes a way for whoever sent it to read my inbox. The permission controls I had asked me to decide about each tool: allow it, deny it or ask every time. None of those answers was right, because the risk didn't belong to any one tool. It belonged to what the session had done before the call. So I built TaintGuard , a Claude Code mod that records what kind of content has entered a session and restricts later tool calls based on that history.

articles.title: A One-File On-Page SEO Check You Can Run Before You Hit Publish
articles.excerpt: Most SEO slips are boring ones: a page with no meta description, two H1s, images without alt text, a title that gets cut off in results. They are easy to fix and just as easy to forget when you are ed…
articles.body: Most SEO slips are boring ones: a page with no meta description, two H1s, images without alt text, a title that gets cut off in results. They are easy to fix and just as easy to forget when you are editing at the end of a long day. I wrote a small Hermes skill, seo-page-audit , that checks those basics on a single URL or a local HTML file. It is one Python file using only the standard library, so there is nothing to install and no API key. It reads the HTML, then lists issues ranked high, medium or low: missing title or description, no H1 or several, heading level jumps, canonical, lang, viewport, noindex, Open Graph tags, image alt and dimensions, links with no text, and a rough word count. The exit code is 1 when there is a high-priority issue, so you can drop it into a CI step.

articles.title: Nostalgia: This phone spoke to me like no other
articles.excerpt: Camera in a smartphone body.
articles.body: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority I might be a bit jaded, but smartphones have become a bit boring. Don’t get me wrong, modern flagships are incredible pieces of technology. But across the board, what you get in terms of year-over-year upgrades are faster processors, better cameras, and slightly brighter screens, but there’s rarely a phone that makes me stop and go, “Wow.” Now that the market is more or less commoditized, I don’t think we’ll ever see that again. However, things were different a decade ago. Phone makers were experimenting with everything from modular designs to 3D displays. Some of those ideas were downright terrible, while others got folded into smartphones we have today. For me, no phone embodied that spirit quite like the Nokia Lumia 1020.

articles.title: 39 Years Later, Calvin And Hobbes' Best Quote On Grief Is Still a Heartbreaking Classic
articles.excerpt: There's a lot more punch in this punchline than your usual Calvin and Hobbes comic strip
articles.body: Most of the time, Bill Watterson's Calvin and Hobbes was a straightforward comedy, set in equal parts a nondescript American suburb and its protagonist's imagination. While it's got more than its share of memorable lines and genuine wisdom, C&H was rarely out to tug on anyone's heartstrings. There are two exceptions to that rule. One is a full story arc from March 1987, in which Calvin tries to rescue a baby raccoon. The other is a one-shot from late in the comic's run, as one of Watterson's more experimental Sunday strips. Both are quiet meditations on death, as Calvin confronts mortality through encounters with animals.

articles.title: New Android exploit only needs you to install an app to wreck your phone
articles.excerpt: Android sabotages itself next.
articles.body: TL;DR Bitdefender researchers discovered an Android vulnerability that can trigger an endless crash loop simply by installing a specially crafted APK, potentially leaving devices unusable. The flaw exploits how Android handles ZIP compression methods, repeatedly crashing the core system_server process. Recovering may require a factory reset or manually deleting the malicious file using ADB. No in-the-wild exploitation has been identified, but the public disclosure could make it easier for threat actors to develop an exploit. Even though Android is a relatively safe operating system, with several security measures in place , threat actors’ ingenuity still keeps finding ways to exploit weaknesses.

articles.body: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is framed as a legend retold. It opens on a tapestry depicting Hyrule’s people and places, as a narrator reflects on Link’s journey like it’s a valuable story worth passing down. For Zelda producers Eiji Aonuma and Hidemaro Fujibayashi, a desire to pass the original game down to a younger group of Zelda developers is one of the main reasons this remake exists: “There are much younger developers who are working on this game, and I do think this is a really valuable experience for them to familiarize themselves first with the original Ocarina of Time and then have their own reinterpretation of it,” Aonuma said.

articles.excerpt: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is out now, and so we have confirmation of the full English voice cast for the first time.
articles.body: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is out now, and so we have confirmation of the full English voice cast for the first time. As fans had suspected following the release of official trailers for the game, Matthew Mercer from the Dungeons & Dragons web series Critical Role, reprises his role as Ganondorf from The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom. Prolific voice actor Erica Mendez plays Zelda, and Navi is voiced by Lisa Reimold. While the original Ocarina of Time, released in 1998 on the N64, did not feature any voiced dialogue, the remake features voice acting in its cutscenes. Link, of course, remains silent throughout — as he does in all the Zelda games. The full list, which IGN has verified via the credits, is below.

articles.body: Generated image of NASA’s new X-70 Fractal experimental aircraft, a crewed, rapidly reconfigurable research platform for advanced aviation technologies. On Wednesday, NASA unveiled its newest experimental aircraft, the X-70 Fractal, during the UP.Summit at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. This high-performance, highly adaptable research platform is designed to accelerate the development and testing of advanced aviation technologies.  The crewed X-70 features advanced, rapidly reconfigurable flight-control technology that will allow NASA to explore aircraft maneuverability in ways never before demonstrated in crewed flight.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 4, 2015: A rail-launched Super Strypi rocket carrying 13 baby satellites failed during its debut launch for the US Air Force
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 4, 2015, the United States Air Force launched an experimental Super Strypi rail-launched rocket carrying 13 tiny satellites, but it failed just after liftoff from Hawaii.
articles.body: On Nov. 4, 2015, the United States Air Force planned to launch an experimental rocket for small satellites from the Pacific Missile Range Facility off Barking Sands, Kauai, Hawaii. The launch didn't according to plan . For this mission, the Air Force was testing out the Super Strypi rocket . The rocket used a rail to help with the liftoff. Super Strypi left the ground, but the rocket quickly spun out of control. When it crashed, it destroyed all of the tiny satellites riding aboard the rocket. The cause? Likely a problem with the first stage motor. The mission lost 13 tiny satellites known as cubesats. Cubesats are a popular option for space missions, because they are small and cheap, and they often operate in swarms.
